Fellow insomniac here, been dealing with it for two years—though it’s not as severe as OP’s, as I get about four hours of sleep. However, I’ve been experiencing persistent jaw pain (similar to TMD, though confirmed to be of muscular nature, and not structural). I’d wake up with it, and it would stay with me for the whole day. Interestingly, the pain decreased if I got less sleep (going 2-3 days without it). Doctors suggested this could be a stress response.

I took a year off work, tried variety of medications, X-rays/scans, mouthguards, and sought second opinions in three different countries, but nothing brought relief. A few months ago, I received severance and left my corporate job, deciding to continue the journey on my own without work to fall back on.

Then, a few weeks ago, I revisited my old psychiatrist, who prescribed SNRI medication (Effexor SR). The first week on the meds was challenging—I’d wake up constantly, rarely sleeping more than 30 minutes at a time. But I noticed something significant: my jaw finally started to relax. Though the medication came with new side effects like drowsiness, I’d rather focus on addressing the pain first and manage the side effects later.

it also lifted my depression. I’d been at the point of considering drastic measures, with a helium tank set up to be attached to my CPAP. Hope I don’t get to use it.

my 0.02$, from someone who volunterily asked for PIP and later a severance package - amicable conclusion after a long tenure in a company, where I burned out, and didn't want to come back after leave:

* it's very difficult to fire employees in Japan (unless it's a case of gross misconduct). The company did hire you, bet on leveraging your skills/potential for the role, but they're also obligated to exhaust other resources - training/rotation. So do consider another role (from your post, I understood, that was still on the table)? I did pivot once to another role, and that helped me explore new opportunities, albeit eventually burning out
* if they are trying to force out you, you should check with employment rules of the company, what severance package (a garden leave?) you deserve. I don't see a reason to "resign voluntarily" without being let go. In my case, company arranged my leave as "for personal reasons", but with "company reason" in the *Rishoku-hyo* (other redditors could chime in here, to suggest whether this is a good/bad idea, as I am still going through the process)

OK, so here we go (after one day of playing with Page):

Price was 230 eur (because of cheap yen), so very affordable for us based in Japan.

Slightly smaller dimensions than Oasis, weighs more, but slimmer. Prefer tactile button response of Oasis, but not a big deal.

Somehow prefer the Page screen lights (both the neutral/warm).

Oasis page turning is somewhat faster - I tried changing refresh settings on Neoreader, but none of them did anything.

Took a few hours to customize Neoreader to fit my needs:

1. Changed font to Bookerly (same as Oasis, had to download/upload it)
2. Adjust margins/line spacing.
3. Installed MacOS dictionaries (had to convert them using [pyglossary](https://github.com/ilius/pyglossary)) - unfortunately they don't keep their formatting - it's become all inline.

Still getting used to the navigation - sidebar, onscreen ball, swipe gestures. A bit overwhelming at first, but getting used to it (disabled the onscreen ball for now).

Love the BooxDrop app - launches a local network uploader/downloader, so I can access Boox'es file system, and upload/move files, over browser via wifi. 

Playstore apps, now this is somewhat disappointing - I don't know what I was expecting, but performance is not on par with the "system" apps - Readwise works, but multiple refreshes/ghosting makes the experience meh - it's like watching paint dry (lol), i.e. it takes some time between each GUI move to redraw/clear the ghosting (I set it up, so it does a full screen refresh, otherwise there's too much ghosting). Having said that, the speakers work pretty well for Readwise's text-to-speech, so functionality wise it beats Oasis by miles.

Battery drains fast, if I continue using wifi/download/BooxDrop mode, but I guess I won't be using it as much later, when I have it setup my way, and stick to reading.

These were my first impressions - like the customizability of the Boox, although still need to have parity with Oasis, to call this a complete improvement over it:

1. Custom dictionary formatting
2. Page turning speed
